scope: Six priority capabilities for architects. This is a curated starting catalog, not an exhaustive inventory of every Copilot preview. Discovery candidates require review before admission.

dynamic-workflows: Pause complex reviews for human approval
copilot-memory: Reuse cited context across code reviews
autopilot: Handle repetitive refactors in a sandbox
Iterate on a task before human review

features.name: Computer Use
features.tagline: Give legacy desktop workflows an agent-assisted runway.
features.summary: Copilot can inspect and operate desktop application controls when an API, MCP server, filesystem tool, or dedicated browser tool is not a better fit.

lifecycle.note: Public preview in local Copilot CLI and Copilot app sessions on Windows and macOS.

value: Assist with GUI-only tasks in legacy software without building an integration first.
Turn a narrowly scoped natural-language request into an observable sequence of app actions.
Demonstrate a permission boundary before discussing broader automation.

enablement.title: Confirm enterprise policy
enablement.detail: The platform owner must permit computer use. Managed features.computerUse can block it; local preferences cannot override that block.

enablement.title: Inspect and enable in a local session
enablement.detail: Use an approved Copilot CLI version on Windows or macOS. Review permissions and grant access only for the synthetic demo app and current session.

enablement.title: Bound the target and stopping condition
enablement.detail: Name the exact app and synthetic document. On macOS, OS Accessibility and Screen Recording permission may be required. Esc twice interrupts CLI activity.

cost.headline: Copilot license + model usage; do not assume GUI actions are free.
cost.detail: Enterprise Copilot CLI model interactions consume AI credits. The reviewed computer-use documentation does not quote a separate computer-use tariff. Check the actual tenant and model usage before quoting a demo cost.
assumptions: Existing approved Copilot seat.
Synthetic local document; no paid external application transaction.
AI credits are usage-based; one enterprise AI credit equals USD 0.01.

limitations: Application versions, focus, timing, accessibility quality, and dynamic controls can change results.
Visible content or screenshots can include sensitive data; close unrelated windows.
Saved Always allow app approval persists across CLI and app; removing it does not revoke an already active session.
A successful fixture test is not a live test of Computer Use or enterprise policy enforcement.

readiness.reason: Public preview, supported platforms, and enablement commands are documented.
readiness.next: Record the exact client version and eligible pilot identity.

readiness.reason: Managed features.computerUse and tool deny rules are documented, but the customer's enforcement has not been tested.
readiness.next: Demonstrate a policy denial on a separate test identity.

readiness.reason: App access follows the active permission mode; desktop actions can inherit the signed-in user's app rights.
readiness.next: Use an isolated OS profile, minimal app rights, and session-only consent.

readiness.reason: Accessible content and visual context may expose information in application windows.
readiness.next: Approve data classification and screen capture; use synthetic data only for the demo.

readiness.reason: Session approvals and interruption are available; permission mode and saved approvals affect prompting.
readiness.next: Test interruption and deny high-impact actions; do not use allow-all.

readiness.reason: Tool activity is visible in the session, not evidence of a complete enterprise audit log.
readiness.next: Capture a permitted trace and map retention, export, identity, and audit gaps.

readiness.reason: AI-credit billing is documented; scenario-specific usage has not been measured.
readiness.next: Measure the rehearsal and approve a tenant budget.

readiness.reason: CLI model access and connected desktop apps can cross different network boundaries.
readiness.next: Validate proxy and app egress separately; do not treat app consent as a network boundary.

readiness.reason: Public-preview risks and UI variability are explicit.
readiness.next: Name a pilot owner and demonstrate a manual fallback after interruption.

readiness.reason: CLI disable and scoped local reset are available; saved app approvals require separate review.
readiness.next: Close the synthetic app, reset the fixture, disable computer use, and review saved approvals.

demo.title: A safer service-desk handoff
demo.prompt: Use Computer Use to interact with the native text editor containing support-brief.txt. Inspect the document first. Change only 'Status: Draft' to 'Status: Ready for pilot' and 'Next step: Unassigned' to 'Next step: Validate policy in test tenant.' Save only this synthetic document to its existing path. Do not access other apps, send anything, change permissions, or use shell/filesystem tools to perform the edits. Stop if the target app or document is ambiguous.
demo.expected: Two exact text changes in the synthetic document, visible app/tool activity, and no external side effect.
demo.remoteCleanup: Disable /computer; review any saved app approvals separately. A local reset cannot revoke permissions in an active session.

features.name: Dynamic Workflows
features.tagline: Coordinate specialist agents with durable, inspectable steps.
features.summary: An experimental Copilot SDK API for extension-authored, session-scoped workflows using subagents, pipelines, journaled steps, pause/resume, and observable run state.

lifecycle.note: Official SDK documentation calls the API experimental. This is not GitHub Actions or a verified public-preview SKU.

value: Split a bounded architecture review into independent, specialist assessments.
Pipeline each item without waiting for a barrier between every stage.
Inspect a run and resume from durable checkpoints rather than starting over.

enablement.title: Verify experimental execution eligibility
enablement.detail: The SDK guide states that execution requires eligible credentials, such as token-based billing or trusted HMAC authentication. Registration alone is not proof that a run is allowed.

enablement.title: Load the included extension
enablement.detail: The .github/extensions/runway-demo extension registers runway-architecture-review using defineWorkflow and joinSession. It does not start an agent or request a secret on load.

enablement.title: Inspect the tool-free specialist profile
enablement.detail: The workflow explicitly selects .github/agents/runway-assessor.agent.md with tools: []. Confirm the profile is loaded and its effective tools are disabled before a live run; a prompt alone is not a tool-access boundary.

enablement.title: Request a bounded demo run explicitly
enablement.detail: Use the runbook's two synthetic applications. Choose and approve runtime/spend limits before an AI run. If dynamic_workflows_unavailable is returned, stop and use the clearly labelled offline rehearsal.

cost.headline: Subagent model usage is real spend, including retries.
cost.detail: AI credits cover the workflow subagent tree. The documented maxAiCredits ceiling is soft and post-paid, so parallel work can settle above it. Schema retries count as additional admitted subagents. No guessed runtime budget is declared in the demo extension.
assumptions: An execution-eligible account and compatible SDK.
Two synthetic application inputs; no nested workflows.
Presenter chooses an approved per-run limit; limits are not an enterprise billing hard stop.

limitations: Experimental API; do not call it public preview solely because the SDK documents it.
Workflow-owned agents use workflow observability rather than ordinary read_agent/write_agent tools.
Ordinary failed agent results can be null; hard runtime failures reject the run.
Journaled steps are best-effort at-least-once; stable keys must include input identity and semantic version.

readiness.reason: The official SDK documents an experimental API and credential-based execution eligibility.
readiness.next: Record a compatible client/SDK and demonstrate admission with the pilot identity.

readiness.reason: The reviewed workflow guide does not establish a dedicated enterprise disable/rollout policy for this API.
readiness.next: Obtain an enforceable control and test it; generic CLI policy is not proof of feature-specific governance.

readiness.reason: Execution eligibility is checked. Without a restrictive profile, subagents can inherit tools/context; this demo explicitly selects a tool-free specialist.
readiness.next: Review extension provenance, verify the effective tools: [] profile, and inspect credentials/context before a live run.

readiness.reason: Durable SQLite-backed workflow storage is described; the reviewed guide does not resolve customer retention, deletion, or residency obligations.
readiness.next: Document journal data flow, storage location, retention, and authorized deletion before customer data.

readiness.reason: Durable pause checkpoints are available. SDK-initiated runs do not themselves request permission.
readiness.next: Keep explicit run authorization, a review checkpoint, and no high-impact side effects.

readiness.reason: Run, phase, progress, and failure observation APIs are documented.
readiness.next: Validate retention, redaction, and incident reconstruction in the target tenant.

readiness.reason: Cumulative limits and soft AI-credit ceilings are documented, not a guarantee of capped billed spend.
readiness.next: Approve per-run ceilings and test tenant-level cost controls.

readiness.reason: A workflow can coordinate agents that use session tools; its DSL is not an egress boundary.
readiness.next: Use the approved sandbox and verify each tool's destinations.

readiness.reason: Resume, cancellation, admission errors, and storage failure are described; the API remains experimental.
readiness.next: Accept experimental support risk and rehearse failure, null-result, and resume cases.

readiness.reason: Cancel and pause APIs are documented; local fixture reset does not erase durable workflow history.
readiness.next: Cancel active runs and review journal cleanup separately; never delete the whole session store.

demo.title: Parallel architecture triage, then human review
demo.prompt: Inspect the registered runway-architecture-review workflow and demos/dynamic-workflows/README.md. Use only the two synthetic applications in the runbook. Explain the exact run arguments, account eligibility, and requested limits; do not start it until I approve this specific run. Stop on dynamic_workflows_unavailable. Pause at the human-review checkpoint, show the run ID and assessments, and do not resume until I approve.
demo.expected: Two independently labelled assessments; the unaudited app is blocked. A paused run resumes with the same ID and cached assessments.
demo.remoteCleanup: Cancel any active workflow by its exact run ID. Reset only local fixture files; retained workflow journals are separate state.

automatedReview.reason: Weekly reassessment. The pinned SDK doc still says the API is experimental, with execution gated on eligible credentials. No lifecycle change is shown. Every gate stays unknown; human dates are not renewed. This is the session SDK API, not GitHub Agentic Workflows.

findings.reason: The doc says experimental and requires eligible credentials. Tested client version, tenant eligibility, and a pilot cohort are not in the fetch.
findings.next: Record client version and test an eligible and an ineligible identity.

findings.reason: The fetched doc shows no enterprise policy or managed setting that disables the API.
findings.next: Find an official policy source and run a negative enforcement test.

findings.reason: Credential eligibility is described, but not scopes, ownership, or revocation.
findings.next: Document credential owner, scopes, and revocation; test out-of-scope denial.

findings.reason: Journal and checkpoint persistence is mentioned, but retention, deletion, and residency are not in the fetch.
findings.next: Review journal contents, retention, and deletion with synthetic data.

findings.reason: No approval boundary or prompt-injection test evidence is in the fetch.
findings.next: Test an untrusted instruction and confirm pause or cancel controls.

findings.reason: Run state and logs are mentioned, but identity mapping, retention, and access control are not shown.
findings.next: Reconstruct a synthetic run and record trace gaps.

findings.next: Cite current billing docs and measure a rehearsal run.

findings.reason: No endpoint, proxy, or egress evidence is in the fetch.

features.name: GitHub Agentic Workflows
features.tagline: Repository automation that reasons, with reviewable outputs.
features.summary: Write agent instructions in Markdown with YAML frontmatter; gh aw compiles them into GitHub Actions workflows with read-only agent jobs and scoped safe outputs.

lifecycle.note: The official announcement names a technical preview. Recheck current lifecycle before adoption.

value: Keep official preview discovery on a repeatable schedule.
Use an agent for interpretation while deterministic CI builds and deploys the site.
Propose new evidence in a pull request without allowing the agent to publish or merge.

enablement.title: Review Actions and engine prerequisites
enablement.detail: Enable approved Actions and review the compiled lock file. Use an approved gh-aw version; this repository pins and checks v0.86.2.

enablement.title: Compile the checked-in source
enablement.detail: The Markdown and generated lock file are both versioned. Deterministic discovery does not need an AI-engine credential.

enablement.title: Opt in to the paid reasoning step
enablement.detail: An administrator configures approved engine authentication and RUNWAY_AGENTIC_ENABLED=true. The included workflow is intentionally inactive until that opt-in; no secrets are created by setup.

cost.headline: Actions runtime + the selected AI engine's usage.
cost.detail: Copilot-engine inference is governed by its billing entity; other engines have their own provider charges. Private-repository Actions usage can consume included minutes and incur overage. The deterministic daily scan does not call an AI model.
assumptions: GitHub Actions is allowed for this repository.
AI-engine authentication and budget are administrator-owned.
No claim that a scheduled workflow is free or that a PAT supplies unlimited usage.

limitations: Dynamic Workflows and GitHub Agentic Workflows are different execution systems.
Safe outputs reduce risk but do not replace review of tools, network access, and compiled YAML.
The agentic step is opt-in; its presence in source is not evidence of a successful paid live run.
Automated discovery never promotes a gate to pass or silently advances a last-verified date.

features.name: Cloud Sandboxes
features.tagline: Move the execution environment, not your laptop's blast radius.
features.summary: Run an interactive Copilot session in a GitHub-hosted isolated Linux environment, with identity, policy, lifecycle, and usage billing managed by GitHub.

lifecycle.note: Cloud sandboxes are public preview and currently require experimental CLI features.

value: Offload a bounded task to an isolated execution environment.
Separate remote agent execution from the local workstation.
Reuse cloud-agent governance and explicitly account for compute and retained snapshots.

enablement.title: Obtain explicit cloud-sandbox access
enablement.detail: Organization-managed access is disabled by default and must be enabled by the organization or enterprise owner.

enablement.title: Start an interactive cloud session
enablement.detail: Use an approved identity and experimental features. Programmatic -p/-i execution is not supported for a cloud sandbox.

enablement.title: Verify execution and lifecycle
enablement.detail: Use only a synthetic task, confirm the remote Linux environment, review network policy, then stop the session and account for its snapshot.

cost.headline: AI credits + compute + allocated memory + stopped-session storage.
cost.detail: The reviewed official prices are USD 0.000024 per compute second, USD 0.000003 per GiB-second of allocated memory, and USD 0.005 per GiB-month of snapshot storage. A one-hour run assuming 4 GiB costs USD 0.1296 for compute plus memory, before AI usage, storage, taxes, or other charges.
assumptions: 4 GiB is an illustrative allocation, not a promised session size.
Inside a Git repository, its owner is billed; outside a repository, select an approved billable owner.
Cloud product/SKU budgets are separate from bundled AI-credit budgets.
The documented preview trial entitlement ended in July 2026; do not assume a current free allowance.
Stopping execution and deleting a stored snapshot are different lifecycle actions.

limitations: Cloud sandboxing is distinct from lighter-weight local OS sandboxing.
CLI cloud sessions are interactive only and currently experimental.
Stopped sessions retain snapshots and can incur storage charges.
A local cleanup cannot stop or delete a remote sandbox.

features.name: Copilot Memory
features.tagline: Make repository context reusable, without hiding its governance.
features.summary: Copilot stores cited repository facts and user preferences that can inform later supported interactions. Scope, billing-entity ownership, validation, retention, and deletion matter.

lifecycle.note: Public preview across supported Copilot surfaces; repository facts and user preferences have different scopes.

value: Reduce repeated explanations of verified repository conventions.
Reuse repository facts across supported Copilot surfaces.
Make context ownership and deletion a visible part of the adoption story.

enablement.title: Confirm the policy and account preference
enablement.detail: Managed plans require administrator enablement; individual users can opt out. Enablement is per user, not per repository.

enablement.title: Choose the correct scope
enablement.detail: Use a non-sensitive synthetic repository convention with a real code citation. Do not create a user preference as part of this demo.

enablement.title: Inspect before reusing
enablement.detail: Repository facts must be validated against the current branch. Code review uses repository facts, not user preferences.

cost.headline: AI usage applies; no separate Memory price verified.
cost.detail: The reviewed Memory documentation does not specify a standalone memory-storage tariff. The underlying CLI, cloud-agent, and other model interactions still follow their billing model. Do not describe memory as unlimited or free because no separate price is listed.
assumptions: An eligible account with Memory allowed.
One non-sensitive repository fact in a throwaway demo repository.
No personal information, customer information, or user-scoped preference is stored.

limitations: Enablement applies to a user's supported work across repositories, not only a single demo folder.
Repository facts are shared with eligible users of the same repository.
Unused entries expire after 28 days; successful validation/use may reset that timer.
Local reset does not delete server-side memories; delete only the exact demo fact through authorized settings.

readiness.next: Verify the account policy, plan, and billing entity.

readiness.reason: Citations, 28-day unused-entry expiry, and deletion are documented; active use can renew retention.

demo.title: A convention survives a new session
demo.prompt: In the throwaway demo repository, inspect normalize-ticket.mjs. The repository convention is that ticket IDs are lowercase and hyphenated. If Memory is enabled and allowed, capture only that non-sensitive repository fact with a citation to the code. Do not create a user-level preference. Show what was captured. In a new session, use the validated convention to produce ticket.json for the synthetic title 'Demo Ticket'.
demo.expected: A cited, repository-scoped synthetic convention and a generated ticket ID of demo-ticket in a later session.
demo.remoteCleanup: With the repository owner's authorization, delete only this demo fact in repository Settings > Copilot > Memory. Never clear all memories.

features.name: Autopilot Mode
features.tagline: Stay on a bounded objective until the result is verified.
features.summary: An experimental CLI mode that encourages the agent to continue toward a completed objective. Autonomy is not a replacement for permissions, sandboxing, budgets, or output review.

lifecycle.note: The official CLI README lists Autopilot under experimental features; client behavior and limits should be rechecked.

value: Keep a small repair task moving through implementation and verification.
Show the difference between an agent saying done and a measurable passing result.
Demonstrate sandbox and permission boundaries alongside autonomy.

enablement.title: Use the disposable fixture workspace
enablement.detail: Never start this demo from the home folder, customer repository, or a directory containing secrets. Review effective permissions and sandbox support.

enablement.title: Start and inspect experimental mode
enablement.detail: Enable experimental features and inspect available modes. Shift+Tab cycles modes; /autopilot is available in the verified CLI help/release lineage.

enablement.title: Give a narrow objective and review the result
enablement.detail: Use only the seeded discount function and its tests. Do not grant allow-all or permission bypass; stop if the host cannot enforce the required sandbox.

cost.headline: Longer autonomous sessions can consume more model usage.
cost.detail: Current enterprise billing is token-based AI credits, not a fixed promise of one billable request per task. Autonomous work, retries, and frontier models change cost. The README's legacy premium-request text is not used as enterprise pricing evidence.
assumptions: One synthetic task with a measurable test suite.
Approved model, effective tenant budget, and no permission bypass.
A continuation or runtime limit is not evidence of a hard billed-spend cap.

limitations: Experimental behavior can vary by version.
Autonomy can broaden tool activity unless the environment and objective are bounded.
Do not use a completion message as a substitute for running the required tests.
Sandbox availability and enforcement differ by OS; fail closed when required controls cannot be applied.

demo.title: Fix the discount bug, not the test
demo.prompt: Work only in this synthetic demo workspace. Fix discount.mjs so discount(120, 25) is 90, discount(40, 0) is 40, and discount(40, 100) is 0. Reject non-finite or negative prices and percentages outside 0..100. Do not modify discount.test.mjs, install dependencies, access the network, use other directories, or commit/push. Run node --test discount.test.mjs and stop only when all tests pass. If effective policy or required sandboxing blocks a step, stop and explain rather than bypass it.
demo.expected: The seeded tests fail before the repair and pass afterward, with the original test file unchanged.
demo.remoteCleanup: No remote state is created by this kit. Stop the session before local reset and return the CLI to the prior mode/settings.
